compiled_state.description:
Discovered while fixing bug regardable-superduper-whiteeye (dca1-f641-caeb-4df4). That ticket fixed ONE test; this one covers the rest of the class, which was surveyed but deliberately left out of that change to keep its scope honest.

## The class

A test fixture creates a bare git repository with a raw `git init --bare` and pushes into it. At git's defaults a bare repository's `receive-pack` runs `run_auto_maintenance()` after every push, spawning `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` — a background process that OUTLIVES the push. `subprocess.run([... "push" ...], check=True)` returning is therefore NOT a happens-before edge for that repository's object database.

If the test then COPIES or byte-walks that directory, it races a concurrent repack: entries vanish mid-walk and the copy raises. Measured signatures include a vanished `objects/maintenance.lock` (what CI caught) and whole loose-object fanout directories (`objects/2c`, `objects/2d`, ...) being pruned as maintenance packs them.

rebar pins `gc.autoDetach=false` / `maintenance.autoDetach=false` on every store it OWNS (`_commands/init.py`'s gc-config ensure unit; bug 88eb, ADR 0051). A bare remote built by a test fixture is owned by no rebar code, so it runs at git's defaults. That is the gap.

## The established remedy

Pin three keys on the bare repo immediately after creating it, before anything is pushed:

    gc.autoDetach=false
    maintenance.autoDetach=false
    receive.autogc=false

Measured postures (all with `receive-pack` confirmed present in a `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` trace):

| posture | maintenance children | detached? |
|---|---|---|
| git defaults | 1 | yes — background mutator |
| autoDetach pins only | 1 | no — foreground, push waits |
| all three pins | 0 | n/a — no upkeep at all |

Two call sites already do this independently: `_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` / `_init_bare_remote` in `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` (bug 5b74-5d8f-a6b4-4674), and `_BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` / `_init_bare_remote` in `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` (bug dca1). They are byte-identical copies of the same three keys under two different names — which is itself the drift this ticket should end.

## HIGH-risk sites found by the survey (push, then the tree containing the bare repo is copied)

Both reach `clone_topology_template`, which does `shutil.copytree(template, destination, symlinks=True)` (`tests/_topology_template.py:226`) AND a full-tree `rglob("*")` + `read_bytes()` rewrite/verification pass (lines ~155/168 and ~193/200). The bare remote lives INSIDE the copied topology, so both the copy and the verification walk race it.

1. `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py:140` — `_git(remote, "init", "-q", "--bare")` in `_build_backup_fixture`; pushes at 142-143 (`push --all`, `push --tags`); copied at 178 via `clone_topology_template`. No pins anywhere in the file. Worse than the dca1 case: the copytree runs once per test in the module.
2. `tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py:37` — `git init -q --bare` in `_build_repo_with_origin`; `rebar.init_repo(...)` at 44 pushes under the default `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`; copied at 73 via `clone_topology_template`. No pins.

`clone_topology_template` is the amplifier — its own docstring says the topology "may contain multiple ordinary repositories, bare sibling remotes, ...". Any template containing an unpinned bare remote is exposed.

## MEDIUM-risk sites (push into an unpinned bare repo, but no later copy/byte-read of it)

~35 further sites, e.g. `tests/interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py:65` (shared — backs the `repo_with_origin_tickets` fixture used by several store tests), `tests/unit/test_sync_remote_config.py:141,163`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_push_parent_exit.py:69`, `tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py:103`, `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py:216`, `tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:109` (`git clone --bare` then `fetch` / `repack -a -d` / `prune --expire=now`, then served over `git daemon` — a fetch also arms auto-gc). These are not currently known to flake, because nothing copies or byte-compares the remote; they are latent, and become HIGH the moment someone adds a snapshot or copy step.

Verified NOT affected: `tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py`, `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py` — each does `rglob`/`iterdir` over the TRACKER worktree, not the bare remote. `tests/integration/test_stdout_purity.py:50` creates a bare repo but never pushes into it (LOW).

## Approach

1. Extract ONE shared helper — the three pins plus an `init_bare_remote(path)` — into a shared test module (`tests/_git_upkeep.py` or alongside `tests/_topology_template.py`) so `tests/` has a single definition instead of the current two copies. Repoint `test_concurrency_regression.py` and `test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` at it.
2. Fix the two HIGH sites by routing their bare-repo creation through that helper.
3. Consider making `clone_topology_template` itself refuse (or pin) a template containing an unpinned bare remote, so the amplifier cannot silently re-acquire the problem. That is the change that would make this class un-reintroducible rather than merely fixed once.
4. Decide whether the MEDIUM sites are worth a sweep now or are better handled by (3).

Explicitly NOT acceptable as fixes, for the same reasons recorded on dca1: retrying the copy, sleeping before it, or excluding `*.lock` from the walk. The `*.lock` filter in particular is measurably insufficient — the repack limb prunes whole fanout directories, not just lock files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/` contains exactly one definition of the bare-remote upkeep pins; checked by grepping for `receive.autogc` and finding a single assignment site.
- [ ] `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` and `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` both consume that shared definition rather than their own copy; checked by reading the diff.
- [ ] `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py` creates its bare remote with the pins applied before its first push; checked by reading the diff.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py` creates its bare remote with the pins applied before its first push; checked by reading the diff.
- [ ] A push into each newly-pinned remote leaves no detached background upkeep; checked by a test that runs the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and asserts no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control so it cannot pass vacuously.
- [ ] Each newly-pinned site's guard genuinely discriminates; checked by removing the pins and observing RED, then restoring them and observing GREEN.
- [ ] `pytest tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py -q` is green; checked by that command.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (requiring `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) all pass; checked by running each.
compiled_state.title: Unpinned bare fixture remotes let a push leave detached git auto-maintenance racing the next copy
